questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: a new germanspeaking city that i didn't know from before, an that it was a universitycity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A small, and beautiful city, sorrounded by lush nature. Easy to socialize and get in touch with people (if that is wanted), both erasmus/international and germans. Also learned a lot academic-wise, eventhough in general the Uni is very traditional/conservative....

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: easy,

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: got assistance by e-mails, on basically everything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: you recieve more information than you thought you needed

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: it's all about luck, write to everything you come over.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: find housing in Altstadt!!!!! it is a littlebit more expansive, but more than worth it, on different levels. It is a small city, with not the best public-transport in the evening/night. Also you are available and more likely to do different things since it's easy and fast to get to places. also there are a lot of beautiful going for a walk/hiking paths.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i don't know. but there are a lot of students, and therefore a lot of housing. but don't relay on getting a Studentenwerk housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: easy, but not so structured...

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you find what courses you want, then you register, which can vary from teacher to teacher if it is in lsf/moodle, or registering by mail. if you are unsure send a mail to the professor.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: i don't know

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 50/50. the registrationperiod was already ended when us Erasmus was applying, so there were some courses that were already full by participants. so i can recommend to apply for more courses than you need in the begginning, and then you de-registrer at a later point if you have to many.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: send e-mail to the professors, and if you struggle with how to set up the scheme, i think there is an erasmus office that can help you. ask one question tooo much, than one too little :-)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
it seems like it is very up to the professor on what and how to teach, therefore it is a big variation in both what is expected from you, but also what kind of courses offered. Some professors and courses were excellent, but some should not teach, and are only teaching so that they can do research....
It is also a lot more workload than what I am used to. I have never worked so much for so few ECTS. So expect a lot of workload both through the semester and also the exams.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: as i described so different from professors to professors, some really bad and some really high. There where low, middle and high levels.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: very different. in the seminars you are expected to participate every time in discussions in class, which also means you have to read the texts for each time. i had one course with assignments every week, in other courses i was supposed to hand in reading responses, and in the vorlesnung it was a lot less expected, but if you take the final exam in vorlesnung then there is one/two text to read every week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: dont have time for that

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i can really reccoment courses on the Transcultural department (CATS), they have some really nice courses and professors in all from economics to culture.

questions.answer: no money on what you need to read at uni

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: some nice bars, also theater for free, a cinema with good movies, freibad, etc.. don't really know so much about sports, except from great nature around the city (4 free xp)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: jazz-jam at Cave54 every tuesday

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: check out the small cities and villages around the area. it does not take a lot of time, cheap (i think you can go with student-id for free in the weekends), and have great things to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very, they are very international in Heidelberg, and a lot of students live here, so it's easy to blend in if you want

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: just talk to people, ask stupid questions just to get a conversation started, the locals are so warm and open!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the most difficult is to be polite in the German way, when ordering at a bar or sending email to your professor...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: people are so openminded, warm and easy-going

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: enjoy the people and city, it can be overwhelming somethimes, and it's okay to take a break from all the things happening when it is too much - go for a walk then :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: to experience a new culture, both with people and the academia, giving perspectives to what you have at home

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: to be present

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
